Fingerprint a table's values

Source: R/crt_table_fingerprint.R
crt_table_fingerprint.Rd

Computes the value a provenance receipt stores in result.fingerprint for a table: the SHA-256, in lowercase hex, of the table's canonical form. Two tables with the same rows in any order, and the same columns in any order, have the same fingerprint; any changed value changes it, except a double moved less than its declared tolerance's rounding.

Usage

crt_table_fingerprint(x, tolerance = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame.

tolerance

A named numeric vector or list: for each double column that is allowed to move between equivalent builds, its absolute tolerance, a power of ten from 1 to 1e-15. Columns not named are fingerprinted exactly.

Value

A string of 64 lowercase hex digits.

Details

Not crt_schema_fingerprint(), which hashes a table's column names and types and never its values.

The canonical form

The RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {"columns": [...], "rows": [[...], ...]}, so any language with a JCS serializer and SHA-256 reproduces it (crate#43):

  • Columns are sorted by name, as UTF-8 bytes (C collation).

  • Every cell is a JSON string, or null for NA.

  • Character values are their UTF-8 text, not Unicode-normalized; factors are their labels.

  • Integers are their decimal digits; logicals are true and false.

  • A double with a declared tolerance 10^-k is written with exactly k decimals, rounding its exact binary value with ties to even, as C's printf and Python's format(x, ".kf") do. With no tolerance it is written in ECMAScript's shortest round-trip form, so it is exact. A zero is written without a sign. NaN and infinite values abort.

  • Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Datetimes are converted to UTC and written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; one with fractional seconds aborts, so round it or fingerprint it as a number.

  • Rows are sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of each row's own canonical JSON.

Examples

a <- data.frame(segment = c("b", "a"), km = c(12.5, 3.0000000001))
b <- data.frame(km = c(3.0000000002, 12.5), segment = c("a", "b"))

# Different rows order, column order and an 11th-decimal difference
crt_table_fingerprint(a) == crt_table_fingerprint(b)
#> [1] FALSE
crt_table_fingerprint(a, c(km = 1e-9)) == crt_table_fingerprint(b, c(km = 1e-9))
#> [1] TRUE
